source: Scripted from the Kotlin unit tests and ColmiSyncEngine.kt of the upstream Android app; synthetic bytes only

conventions.step: { expectWrite: exact on-air hex, channel?: "command" (big-data requests go to de5bf72a-…; default "write" = 6e400002-…), notify: frames the fake ring sends after that write, notifyChannel?: "bigData" (de5bf729-…; default "notify" = 6e400003-…) }
conventions.action: What the session caller did to cause the write (handshake, liveHeartRate.start, workout.start, syncSleepNow, …). Steps without an action follow from the previous reply or a timer (afterMs).
conventions.expectEvents: Kotlin RingDecodedEvent output for the step's notifications (asserted in the test where the source says so, otherwise derived from the Kotlin source).
conventions.clock: nowMs / tzOffsetS used to build time-dependent frames (set time, HR day requests) and timestamps. Kotlin writes the LOCAL wall clock to the ring.
conventions.ordering: Kotlin queues writes without waiting for replies. A fake ring that answers right after each write produces the same write order.
conventions.startsAfter: History sessions start at the first history request (43 00 0f 00 5f 01), which is also the last write of every handshake session.

sessions.note: Kotlin enqueues every handshake write at once and never waits for a reply; replies are matched by opcode as they arrive. The ring here reports all-day HR on at 5 min and temperature on, so the engine writes nothing back and seeds the config from the replies.

sessions.name: history-walk-empty-cold
sessions.startsAfter: any handshake session (its last write, 43 00 …, is this session's first)
sessions.note: Every day answers "no data" (byte 1 = ff); every big-data reply is empty (length 0). Order: activity 0..7, HR 0..7, stress 0..6, SpO2, sleep, HRV 0..6, temperature (legacy action 37, 6 days because the 0x3C reply did not set supportIntervalTemp). Then the sync is done and nothing more is written.

sessions.name: history-walk-empty-warm-today-only
sessions.source: ColmiSyncEngineGateTest.kt (completed cold pass becomes today only)
sessions.startsAfter: history-walk-empty-cold on the SAME engine (same connection); runStartup is called again
sessions.note: No handshake is repeated on the same engine. In the Android app a reconnect builds a new engine, so every connection starts cold.

steps.note: days 0 is clamped to 1.

sessions.name: hr-log-day-read
sessions.source: ColmiQringParityTest.kt (hr day with data completes at packet size-1 and advances to the next day)
sessions.note: Activity days answer empty to reach the HR stage. HR day 0 has three packets; the request carries the local date at 00:00 UTC and the ring echoes it in packet 1.

steps.note: Packet 0: [15 00 size slotMin]. Packet 1: [15 01 echo u32 LE][9 samples]. Packets 2..size-1: [15 n][13 samples]. 0 = no sample. Packet size-1 ends the day. Samples sit at local midnight + slot * index.
Day 0 complete; the engine asks for day 1 (the session stops here).

sessions.name: steps-day-read
sessions.source: ColmiDecoderTest.kt (activity buckets keep 15-minute slice starts) + ColmiSyncEngine.isTerminalPacket

steps.note: Header packet (byte 1 = f0) is skipped by the Kotlin; its bytes 2..3 are synthetic here (the MIT client reads byte 3 == 1 as "new calorie protocol"). Data packets: BCD date, quarter-hour slot, [5] index, [6] count; the day ends when [5] == [6] - 1. Slot times are LOCAL wall clock.
Day 0 complete; the engine asks for day 1 (the session stops here).

sessions.name: sleep-standalone
sessions.source: ColmiSleepSyncTest.kt (syncSleepNow from idle fires exactly the standalone sleep request; standalone sleep completion does not advance the pipeline)
sessions.startsAfter: idle engine (no history walk running), e.g. after history-walk-empty-cold

steps.note: Main sleep (action 0x27) arrives in 20-byte chunks and is reassembled by the length in bytes 2..3. Start 1380 > end 420, so the night starts 60 min before the local midnight of daysAgo 0. The unsolicited nap record (action 0x3e) uses the same layout and never advances anything.

sessions.name: sleep-in-pipeline
sessions.source: ColmiSleepSyncTest.kt (in-pipeline sleep completion still advances to HRV)

steps.note: In-pipeline sleep completion advances to HRV day 0 (the session stops here).

sessions.name: live-hr-realtime-rejected-fallback
sessions.note: Rings that refuse 0x1e answer 9e ee. The engine remembers the refusal for the life of the connection and runs live HR on the 0x69 stream; while that stream runs it re-sends 69 01 only after 30 s without a 0x69/1 frame (checked every 20 s).

steps.note: The first frame (bpm 0) is warm-up and yields nothing.
The stop carries the last bpm so the ring logs it.
Second session on the same connection: no 0x1e probe.

sessions.name: live-hr-realtime-accepted
sessions.source: ColmiRealtimeHeartRateFallbackTest.kt (a ring that answers 0x1E keeps the realtime path and its continue keepalive)

steps.note: Wall-clock keepalive every 20 s while the stream runs (not per frame).

sessions.name: spot-hr
sessions.source: ColmiEncoder.kt / ColmiSyncEngine.measureHeartRateSpot + stopHeartRate; decode per ColmiDecoderTest.kt (manual heart rate ok)
sessions.note: The caller (RingSyncCoordinator) samples a 30 s window, drops samples in the first 5 s (the ring may echo a cached bpm), then calls stop.

sessions.name: spot-spo2
sessions.source: ColmiQringParityTest.kt (manual spo2 start uses the BCD-25 byte); decode per ColmiDecoder.decodeNormal
sessions.note: SpO2 values outside 70..100 are warm-up and yield nothing; a nonzero error byte yields Spo2Complete. The caller window is 60 s. 6a also stops any 0x69 heart-rate stream.

sessions.name: sport-session-cycle
sessions.source: ColmiSportModeTest.kt (a workout starts a ring-side sport session; ending the workout stops it)
sessions.note: No keepalive: the ring pushes 0x78 on its own (about every 10 s). After 45 s without a push the engine sends one resume (77 03 type); still silent after another 45 s, it sends stop (77 04 type) and falls back to live HR (1e 01). Checked every 20 s.

sessions.name: sport-session-rejected
sessions.source: ColmiSportModeTest.kt (a ring that rejects the sport start falls back to the plain stream, and stays there)
sessions.note: f7 = 0x77 with the error bit (0x80) set: this firmware has no sport sessions; remembered for the connection.

steps.note: Fallback to the plain live-HR stream.
Next workout skips the sport session.

sessions.name: sport-session-ended-by-ring
sessions.source: ColmiSportModeTest.kt (the ring ending the session itself moves the workout onto the plain stream)

steps.note: Status byte 3 = the ring ended this session.
Rest of this workout on live HR; the next workout tries a sport session again.

sessions.name: interval-temperature-paging
sessions.source: ColmiQringParityTest.kt (interval-temp ring pages temperature per day with packet continuation)
sessions.startsAfter: a handshake whose 0x3C reply sets supportIntervalTemp, e.g. 3c reply 3c 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 80 00 00 00 00 00 bc
sessions.note: After a day's last packet the next day starts at packet 0; after day 6 the sync is done. A reply whose packet index does not advance drops to the next day (no re-request loop). A re-emitted frame after done is ignored.

steps.note: Reply header [6] day, [7] interval min, [8] packet count, [9] packet index; samples u16 LE centi-degC on the local-day grid.
Packet 1 continues the slot grid of packet 0 (sample offset 2).
